title: How to wash a finished cross-stitch piece
subtitle: Removing hoop marks and grime without distorting the stitches or bleeding the colours
excerpt: Washing a finished cross-stitch piece removes the hoop ring, chalk marks, and oils transferred from handling. Cold water and a drop of mild soap is enough for most pieces. The risk is colour bleed from dark floss, which can be tested beforehand, and distortion from wringing or tumble drying, which does not happen when the piece is handled flat.
sourceNotes: Fabric care for embroidered textiles. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive, finishing and mounting chapters.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners.
The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Most modern floss is colourfast when washed in cold water; older or very dark colours should be tested first.

content.text: Washing a finished cross-stitch piece is worth doing before framing or mounting. The hoop leaves a ring, hands transfer oils to the fabric during stitching, and chalk or pen grid marks may be visible. Cold water and mild soap remove all of these without harming
. The only caution is colour bleed, which is rare with modern floss but possible with very dark or red shades.

Before washing, test any very dark or red floss for colourfastness. Wet a small scrap of the floss and press it onto a white paper towel. If the colour transfers onto the paper, wash the piece in cold water only (no soap) and keep the water moving to dilute any bleed.

Fill a clean basin with cold water and add a small drop of mild soap (unscented dish soap or a soap formulated for delicates). Submerge the piece and agitate it gently with your fingers. Do not scrub the stitched surface.
Lift the piece out and rinse under cold running water, supporting it flat rather than letting it hang from one corner. Squeeze gently to remove water; do not wring or twist.
Lay the piece face-down on a clean white towel. Roll the towel around it gently to absorb the excess water. Unroll and remove the piece while still damp.

Pin the damp piece to a foam board or ironing board using rustproof pins, pulling it gently square as you pin. Let it dry flat and away from direct sunlight. The fabric should be smooth and flat when fully dry.

items.symptom: The hoop ring does not come out after washing
items.cause: The ring mark is from compression of the threads under the hoop, not from dirt. Washing alone may not remove it.
items.fix: After washing and while the piece is still damp, stretch it gently on a board in the direction of the ring mark and let it dry stretched out. Ironing from the back while the piece is slightly damp also helps; use a pressing cloth over the stitched side.

items.symptom: The fabric puckered and warped after drying
items.cause: The piece was allowed to dry hanging or bunched rather than pinned flat.
items.fix: Re-wet the piece in cold water, remove it flat, and pin it to a board in the correct dimensions before leaving it to dry again.

content.text: A washed and dried piece is ready to iron and mount. Iron from the back, face-down on a clean white towel, using steam. The towel cushions the stitches so they do not flatten under the weight of the iron.
